The '''mee''', also known as a '''daggert''', was a [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]] native to the [[Water/Legends|waters]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. The mee was rotund yet flat, with [[Color/Legends|black]]-and-yellow scales and a set of poisonous spines that protruded from its centerline. With its diagonal striping pattern, it could camouflage itself and blend into its surroundings, such as [[Ocean/Legends|sea]] [[Grass/Legends|grasses]] and reeds. Mee largely resided within [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]], around the underwater [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], and were later transported to Naboo's [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]] in a Gungan recolonization effort, as well as the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] planet [[Aquilaris]].

==Biology and appearance==
Mee, sometimes referred to as daggerts,<ref name="TGF" /> were [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]]<ref name="CSWECite" /> and [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]]<ref name="TGF" /> [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]] native to the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of the<ref name="WSWFG" /> [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="WSWFG" /> but were also found on one of Naboo's [[Moon/Legends|moons]], [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]],<ref name="TGF" /> and the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]<ref name="EAOC" /> planet [[Aquilaris]].<ref name="EIR">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref> The typical mee possessed a rotund though vertically flat body, with [[Color/Legends|black]]-and-yellow scales and poisonous spines that protruded from its centerline.<ref name="WSWFG" /> Its diagonal striping served as camouflage, allowing it to blend into sea [[Grass/Legends|grasses]] and reeds.<ref name="CSWECite" /> Larger varieties of mee known as jumbo daggerts existed in the core of Naboo and were considered much rarer than their surface counterparts.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 9">''[[Episode I Adventures 9: Rescue in the Core]]''</ref>

==Behavior==
[[File:Otta1-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A school of mee is hunted by a pair of [[otta]].]]
Mee [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduced]] frequently, though they possessed a short lifespan. They survived by nibbling at the [[root]]s of [[Plant/Legends|plants]] growing in the [[Water/Legends|water]].<ref name="TGF" /> Mee were plentiful, traveling in schools of thousands, and were a staple food source of many other [[Species/Legends|species]], such as the [[Opee sea killer/Legends|opee sea killer]], [[Faa/Legends|faa]], [[Yobcrab/Legends|yobcrab]], [[Tee/Legends|tee]], [[See/Legends|see]], [[Pikobi/Legends|pikobi]], and [[otta]].<ref name="WSWFG" /> Their diet included [[bubble spore]] and their seeds, [[Cambylictus tree/Legends|cambylictus trees]], [[Chak-root/Legends|chak-root]], [[green glie]], [[nave]], [[pom]], [[red glie]], [[rutiger tree]]s, and [[tassler tree]]s and their knees.<ref name="TGF" />

On Naboo, the mee were commonly found in both shallow and deep [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]],<ref name="TGF" /> and in the area around the underwater [[City/Legends|city]] [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], one of the homes of the [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] species. They were attracted by the underwater city's lights; however, they knew by experience not to go through the portal zones of the [[Hydrostatic bubble/Legends|hydrostatic bubbles]] that led to the [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]]-filled chambers.<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==History==
Mee evolved in the waters of Naboo<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> and were transported in Gungan colonization efforts to its moon Ohma-D'un.<ref name="TGF" /> Some mee were present in the waters of [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]]<ref name="ITWEI">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> as of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> as [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]; his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]; and their Gungan scout, [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], swam to Otoh Gunga to speak with local representatives.<ref name="TPM" />

==Mee in the galaxy==
Circa [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="NEC-Dreadnaughts">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] ''[[Star Wars: Republic: Dreadnaughts of Rendili]]'' to [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> mee, along with [[Ray/Legends|ray]], faa, and [[Laa/Legends|laa]], were present in a holding tank aboard the ''[[Titavian IV]]'', an exploration [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] formerly operated by the [[Intergalactic Zoological Society]] on [[Mycroft]] whose mission was to gather and catalog specimens from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Rendili">[[Republic 69|''Republic'' 69]]</ref> The scalefish were also present on the water planet of Aquilaris.<ref name="EIR" />

Mee were such a notable fish on Naboo that they were included in children's [[holographic nursery mobile]]s<ref name="TCW">{{TCW|Children of the Force}}</ref> around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], lasting from [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Despite their poisonous nature, mee could be consumed by non-aquatic species and were presented as [[Scalefish fillets|fillets]] in [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] located in the [[CoCo Town/Legends|CoCo Town]] district of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="DD">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The mee first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="TPM" /> along with other scalefish named [[Doo/Legends|doo]], ray, faa, [[See/Legends|see]], laa, and tee, which refer to the real-world [[Wikipedia:Solfège|musical scale]]: "Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Ti." All of these fish were first named according to the musical scale in 1999's [[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The mee also appeared in subsequent associated material, including ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'',<ref name="EIR" /> ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier]]'',<ref name="TGF" /> and the [[2000]] [[Daniel Wallace]] short story "[[The Monster]]" in [[Star Wars Gamer 2|''Star Wars Gamer'' 2]].<ref name="The Monster">{{GamerCite|2|The Monster}}</ref>

''The Gungan Frontier'', released two days before ''Episode I: The Visual Dictionary'', gave the mee an alternative name: the daggert, a reference to [[Star Wars video games|game]] developer [[Todd Daggert]], courtesy of ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'' author [[Terryl Whitlatch]].<ref name="Facebook">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|author=[[Terryl Whitlatch|Whitlatch, Terryl]]|date=2014-03-20|url=N/A|archivefile=File:Daggert-whitlatch.png}}</ref> Jumbo daggerts were mentioned in the 2000 young readers novel ''[[Episode I Adventures 9: Rescue in the Core]]''.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 9" /> Later references to the mee were made in a [[2004]] [[Republic 69|issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series<ref name="Rendili" /> and the [[2007]] ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novel [[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice|''Sacrifice'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy of the Force">''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]''</ref> Most recently, two representations of mee made an appearance alongside a see in a [[2009]] [[Children of the Force|episode]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'',<ref name="TCW" /> and mee were also mentioned as "daggerts" in 2009's "[[Dining at Dex's]]," a [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] article.<ref name="DD" />
